title: One, Two & Enough
intro: Toddlers quickly learn to count the things they want and signal when they have enough. Today we add 3 practical quantity sounds for shops, ticket counters, and meals, then combine them with earlier lessons.

words.babyAnalogy: Holding up one finger while choosing a single treat.
words.actionTag: At a bakery or tea stall, hold up one finger and say 'Ondu kodi' (Give me one).

words.babyAnalogy: Holding up two fingers to ask for a pair of things.
words.actionTag: When buying two tickets or two items, show two fingers and say 'Eradu beku' (I need two).

words.babyAnalogy: Covering the bowl with a hand when no more food is wanted.
words.actionTag: When a server has given you enough food, raise your palm gently and say 'Saaku'.

combos.context: Combining Ondu (Lesson 5) + Kodi (Lesson 4) at a shop or food counter.

combos.meaning: That's enough; I don't want more.
combos.context: Combining Saaku (Lesson 5) + Beda (Lesson 2) to stop another serving.

quiz.scenario: At a bakery, you point to a bun and want exactly one.
quiz.question: What do you say while holding up one finger?
quiz.explanation: Ondu (One) + Kodi (Give politely, Lesson 4) = Give me one, please.

quiz.scenario: At a ticket counter, you are buying for yourself and a friend.
quiz.question: How do you say that you need two?
quiz.explanation: Eradu (Two) + Beku (Need, Lesson 2) = I need two.

quiz.scenario: A server keeps adding rice to your plate, but you already have enough.
quiz.question: What phrase politely signals that you want no more?
quiz.explanation: Saaku (Enough) + Beda (Don't want, Lesson 2) = That's enough; I don't want more.
